rationale: Amendment applied: .ufo/waves/round-23/preseal-amendment.md, 'C2 final rules superseding only erroneous/ambiguous original clauses'. DELTA FROM THE ORIGINAL PROPOSAL (cases-proposed/CaseXfsAccountingOnly.json): the only fixture change is the btrfs_sysfs UUID record, which gains the newly required member 'qgroups_enabled' (amendment: 'Add required fixture member qgroups_enabled to each btrfs_sysfs UUID record: true/false/null'; 'qgroups false must pair with enabled=null/mode=null'); that record is a structural decoy (qgroups=false, enabled=null, mode=null) and no btrfs path is queried, so it cannot affect this expectation. The mountinfo text, the paths list, the device_links map and the expected object are carried over unchanged from the original proposal; the expected object is unchanged because the amendment's XFS precedence clause resolves this fixture the same way the original contract row 3 did. RE-DERIVATION UNDER THE AMENDMENT. Step 1, mount resolution (amendment: 'ignore empty trailing lines'; 'Longest component-prefix selection remains'; 'if ANY covering mountpoint occurs more than once, refuse classification as unknown/n/a/ambiguous_overmount'): the mountinfo text ends with a newline, so its final split element is empty and is ignored; the mount points present are /, /home, /run, /tmp and /srv/xfsacct, each occurring exactly once, so no covering mount point is duplicated and the ambiguous_overmount refusal does not fire; for realpath /srv/xfsacct/data the covering mount points are / (explicitly a candidate) and /srv/xfsacct (component-prefix candidate), and the longest wins, so mount_point is /srv/xfsacct. Step 2, per-line field parse (amendment: 'Parse separator and the last THREE fields of EACH chosen line, never file-wide'; 'Octal-decode root, mountpoint and source with exactly 040/011/012/134; reject other backslash escapes as QUOTA_SETUP'): the chosen line '251 33 259:3 / /srv/xfsacct rw,nosuid,nodev,noatime shared:214 - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p3 rw,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=256k,uqnoenforce,pqnoenforce' has separator '-', and its last three fields are fstype 'xfs', source '/dev/nvme0n1p3' and super options 'rw,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=256k,uqnoenforce,pqnoenforce'; root '/', mount point and source contain no backslash at all, so the octal decode is a no-op and no escape is rejected. Step 3, device check (amendment: 'Device mismatch PREEMPTS the filesystem table: unknown/n/a/device_mismatch; device_check=mismatch. Btrfs skips equality only when stat major is 0; nonzero btrfs stat major mismatching the mount -> device_mismatch. Equal -> match.'): the chosen fstype is xfs, not btrfs, and the mount's major:minor 259:3 equals the path's st_dev 259:3, so device_check is match and the filesystem table is reached; the btrfs stat-major-is-0 exemption is irrelevant to an xfs path. Step 4, XFS precedence (amendment: 'XFS precedence: conflict(noquota with ANY quota/enforcement or noenforce key), then noquota, then any enforced key, then any accounting-only key, else absent. Mixed enforced/noenforce means SOME quota-type enforcement flag is set, not all.'): comma-splitting the chosen line's super options and taking the text before '=' gives the keys rw, inode64, logbufs, logbsize, uqnoenforce, pqnoenforce. Step 4.1 (conflict) does not fire because 'noquota' is absent, so there is no noquota-plus-quota-key combination; step 4.2 (noquota) does not fire; step 4.3 (any enforced key: usrquota,uquota,quota,grpquota,gquota,prjquota,pquota) does not fire, because the only quota-related keys present are the accounting-only spellings uqnoenforce and pqnoenforce; step 4.4 (any accounting-only key: uqnoenforce,gqnoenforce,pqnoenforce,qnoenforce) fires, so quota_state is enabled, enforcement is accounting_only and basis is xfs_quota_option; step 4.5 (absent) is not reached. The 'mixed enforced/noenforce' clarification does not apply, since this fixture contains no enforced key at all. Step 5, verdict (amendment keeps the original precedence 'any enabled -> 1 QUOTA_ENABLED'): the single path is enabled, so exit is 1 and finding_id is QUOTA_ENABLED. Source anchors (unchanged from the original proposal; S077 = Documentation/admin-guide/xfs.rst at v7.2 lines 171-185, 'noquota' 171-173 'Forcibly turns off all quota accounting and enforcement within the filesystem.', 'uquota/usrquota/uqnoenforce/quota' 175-177 'User disk quota accounting enabled, and limits (optionally) enforced.', 'gquota/grpquota/gqnoenforce' 179-181, 'pquota/prjquota/pqnoenforce' 183-185, sha256 53bda67b5612a3f2c02820604d05825c9d37addba9855e1d4fba330a516d051c; S078 = fs/xfs/xfs_super.c at v7.2, xfs_showargs lines 238-254 where ',usrquota' is printed only under XFS_UQUOTA_ENFD (238-239), ',uqnoenforce' under XFS_UQUOTA_ACCT (240-241), ',prjquota' under XFS_PQUOTA_ENFD (243-244), ',pqnoenforce' under XFS_PQUOTA_ACCT (245-246), ',grpquota' (248-249), ',gqnoenforce' (250-251) and ',noquota' only when !(mp->m_qflags & XFS_ALL_QUOTA_ACCT) (253-254), with the matching parser arms at 1542-1576 where Opt_uqnoenforce sets XFS_UQUOTA_ACCT and clears XFS_UQUOTA_ENFD and Opt_pqnoenforce does the same for the project scope, sha256 0a95697dcfcdab8f7ab6ea26fdb941db952db4b73ed93c30d21e40861ed0450c; S082 = Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst at v7.2 section 3.5 lines 1965-1990, field table 1970-1983 (major:minor field 3 at 1975, mount point field 5 at 1977, mount options field 6 at 1978, separator m+1 at 1980, filesystem type m+2 at 1981, mount source m+3 at 1982, super options m+4 at 1983), sha256 e760f716f8278deefab17a63739033cadc7faee93663c49e76455afaaf40d126). The kernel anchors show the fixture string is kernel-realistic: the kernel emits exactly one name per active quota scope and prints ',noquota' iff no accounting flag is set, so a mount with user and project accounting but no enforcement reports exactly 'uqnoenforce,pqnoenforce' and never 'noquota'. The btrfs and tmpfs lines in the fixture are structural decoys that make the mount resolution non-trivial; they are not claimed to reproduce any observed host mount. Nothing here asserts a quota limit, usage, or per-user/group/project state; QUOTA_ENABLED remains a runway-reporting finding, not a failure claim.
